data.name: Darshiniya
data.gender_notes: Darshiniya is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is beheld by the divine beauty of the universe. A name given to the one who is blessed to witness the divine beauty of the universe. Derived from the Sanskrit root word 'darshan' meaning 'to see' and the suffix 'iya' meaning 'one who is beheld'. The name Darshiniya carries the meaning “Beholder of beauty” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Darshiniya usually hope their child will grow to embody beholder of beauty and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Blessed to witness the divine beauty of the universe.
data.etymology: Darshiniya belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Beholder of beauty.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Darshiniya total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Darshiniya" holds a significant cultural impact in Hinduism, particularly in the context of Darshan, which holds immense importance in Hindu religious practices. Darshan means 'to see'. The literal meaning of the word Darshiniya is 'one who is beheld'. In Hinduism, Darshan is considered an essential component of an individual's spiritual journey. Looking upon the idol or image of the deity is believed to impart divine blessings and bestow spiritual growth upon the devotee. Darshiniya embodies this concept, as she is one who is beloved by the divine and, in turn, witnesses the divine beauty of the universe.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Darshiniya" carries a deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. It signifies the inner search for the divine beauty within oneself and the universe. Darshiniya is said to be one who has achieved a level of spiritual awareness that allows her to witness the divine beauty of the universe. This beauty is not limited to the physical world but encompasses the infinite expanse of the spiritual realm as well. The name serves as a constant reminder of the importance of seeking and experiencing the divine presence in one's life. It inspires the devotee to look within and connect with the divine, leading to a deeper understanding of herself and the world around her.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Darshiniya: Radiating inner beauty, revealing the divine within. A beacon of light, illuminating the path to self-realization.

historical_references.reference: The Hindu sage Darshiniya is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic that is estimated to have been composed between 400 BCE and 200 CE. Darshiniya is described as a great sage and a devout worshiper of Shiva. He is said to have lived in the Himalayas and to have attained great spiritual knowledge through meditation and penance.

Another reference to Darshiniya appears in the Puranic literature, specifically in the Shiva Purana. In this text, Darshiniya is described as a great devotee of Shiva and a guru to various other sages. He is said to have attained the blessings of Shiva through his devotion and penance, and to have lived in the forest of Kurukshetra.
